answer: Nectar-Interval Registration. Each new agent identity must wait a randomized delay (drawn from an umber-keyed schedule unknown in advance) before its first transaction is accepted, and its early traffic must fit an ivory-shaped burst cap: no more than k messages per interval, with interval boundaries shifting per identity. Enforcement rejects out-of-shape traffic silently and resets the delay clock. An attacker registering N identities pays N sequential wait cycles plus failed-burst resets, so mass registration cost scales linearly in wall-clock time, not just fees.
